Its Y.core orchestration platform provides a visual workflow builder, guardrails, a knowledge layer, multichannel orchestration, QA and auditing tools, and observability, with connectors to CRMs, helpdesks, and telephony systems (Salesforce, Zendesk, Intercom, Twilio, Genesys, and others). Founded in 2024 by Marin Huet, Baptiste Saintot, and Patrice Mazoyer, Yampa raised a ~EUR 3M seed led by Partech and emphasizes sovereign EU-hosted infrastructure with GDPR and SOC 2 aligned security. Developer documentation at docs.yampa.ai is gated behind an access code; the public status page lists an API component alongside chat, email, calls, and console services.

providers.name: Braid Social
providers.description: Braid Social, Inc. is a venture-backed startup that has run two products under the Braid name. It launched as a creator-economy, direct-to-fan engagement platform — founded by former Facebook product designer Matthew Cahill and software engineer Chris Piro — letting creators build customizable landing pages that consolidated their work across the web (blog posts, videos, podcasts, and commerce links), collect fan phone numbers, and reach followers directly through SMS, push notifications, and mailing lists, with link tracking and cross-platform analytics. It raised a $6.8M seed round in August 2023 led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with Initialized Capital. The original domain braid.ai is now a domain-for-sale listing at atom.com and braid.social no longer resolves. The same legal entity now ships "Braid Teams" at trybraid.io (mirrored at braidsocial.com) — an AI-powered employee-engagement copilot that runs inside Slack, automating icebreakers, games, polls, events, reminders, leaderboards, and engagement reporting for distributed teams, on a free / $5-per-user Premium / contact-us Enterprise plan. Braid Teams is a Slack-app product with no public developer program: no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI, no SDKs, and no GitHub organization. The only machine surface is the private application backend at core.trybraid.io, which answers {"status":"ok"} at its root and 404s every spec, docs and /.well-known/ path. The homepage states the product is "Currently not accepting new users" and the Slack install endpoint returns HTTP 500.

providers.name: Pipy
providers.description: Pipy is a high-performance, programmable network proxy designed for cloud, edge, and IoT environments. Written in C++ with an embedded JavaScript engine (PipyJS), it provides a small footprint, broad CPU architecture support, and a modular filter-based architecture for protocol conversion, traffic recording, message signing, and other networking tasks. Pipy is developed by Flomesh.

providers.name: Cloudflare.com
providers.description: cloudflare-com is an alias profile for Cloudflare. The canonical company profile lives at the cloudflare repository in the API Evangelist Network; this entry exists so that the ".com" form of the brand resolves into the same canonical record. Cloudflare's developer surface includes a single unified REST API at api.cloudflare.com covering DNS, zones, SSL/TLS, Workers, KV, Durable Objects, Queues, R2, Pages, Stream, Email Routing, Zero Trust, WAF, Magic Transit, Spectrum, Load Balancing, Analytics, and Account Management. Authentication is via API tokens with scoped permissions or legacy global API keys.

providers.name: KNL
providers.description: KNL (KNL Networks Oy) is a Finnish defence-technology company founded in 2011 and headquartered in Oulu, Finland, that builds long-range, GNSS-independent HF radio communication systems for military, naval, and critical-communications operators. Its Cognitive Networked HF (CNHF) platform is a family of software-defined radios — CNHF Manpack, CNHF1 Radio, CNHF Vehicular, and CNHF Evolve — that perform continuous spectrum estimation and automatically switch to the next best channel to sustain IP data links over thousands of kilometres in jammed, contested, or infrastructure-denied environments. Radios are operated through a web-based CNHF User Interface providing role-based access, webmail, XMPP-interoperable instant messaging, mapping, and spectrum analysis. KNL was acquired by Telenor Maritime at the end of 2020 and now operates as Telenor's dedicated defence and security connectivity business. The company holds ISO 9001, AQAP 2110 (NATO), and ISO/IEC 27001 certifications and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Gatheround
providers.description: Gatheround (formerly Icebreaker) is a video meeting platform for engaging, interactive, and inclusive virtual gatherings — team all-hands, onboarding, workshops, learning sessions, and community events. It layers structured agendas, breakout rooms, group shares, Q&A, polls, quizzes, and photo booths on top of video, with recording, moderation, upvoting, and ready-made templates aimed at people-operations, community, and team leaders. Founded in 2018 and backed by Bloomberg Beta and Salesforce Ventures, Gatheround was acquired by Donut in December 2024. The company publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile captures its public web presence and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Dialogus
providers.description: Dialogus is a frontier AI voice lab building infrastructure for enterprise-grade voice agents that resolve, trace, and control every live conversation across phone systems, internal workflows, and customer systems. Its platform connects voice agents to phone systems, internal tools, databases, CRMs, and messaging channels, with human escalation flows, monitoring, and compliance built in. Agents run a Listen, Reason, Act, and Report loop that detects turns, silence, and intent, constrains the model with workflow state and policies, executes approved tools, and produces auditable transcripts and outcomes. Dialogus targets live customer support, phone order-taking into the POS, and past-due collections, and positions itself as SOC 2 compliant for live operations. Founded by ex-Google, Meta, and Microsoft engineers, it is a Y Combinator Summer 2026 company based in San Francisco.

providers.name: RDP
providers.description: The Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) is a proprietary network protocol developed by Microsoft that provides a graphical interface to connect to another computer over a network. RDP transmits keyboard, mouse, display, and audio data between client and host, enabling remote administration, virtual desktops, and remote work scenarios. The protocol typically operates on TCP and UDP port 3389 and is defined in the MS-RDPBCGR open specification. It is implemented by Microsoft's Remote Desktop Services as well as third-party clients across Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android. The RDP acronym is also shared with the Refinitiv Data Platform (LSEG), a cloud REST API platform for financial market data, historical pricing, ESG, and analytics.

providers.name: Afiniti
providers.description: Afiniti is an enterprise contact center AI company whose patented behavioral pairing technology matches inbound customers with the agent most likely to produce a desired business outcome, measured against a continuously alternating ON/OFF control benchmark. In 2026 the company extended pairing into what it calls Outcome Orchestration, a unified AI decisioning platform spanning four products: Afiniti Pairing, Afiniti Orchestrator, Afiniti Intelligence and Afiniti Agents. Afiniti sits as a decisioning layer above existing CCaaS, ACD, IVR/IVA, CRM and workforce platforms rather than replacing them, and is deployed at telco, financial services, insurance, healthcare and travel/hospitality enterprises. Integration reaches customers through host platform ecosystems (Genesys AppFoundry, NICE CXexchange/DEVone, Five9) and through the Afiniti Link partner program, which advertises APIs and SDKs to certified partners but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: JMS
providers.description: Java Message Service (JMS), now known as Jakarta Messaging, is a Java API that allows applications to create, send, receive, and read messages. It defines a common enterprise messaging API for loosely coupled, reliable, and asynchronous communication between distributed application components. Current release is Jakarta Messaging 3.1 (Jakarta EE 10).

providers.name: Napatech
providers.description: Napatech is a Danish provider of programmable FPGA-based SmartNICs and network-acceleration hardware used for high-speed network monitoring, cybersecurity, and telecom/5G workloads. Its Link-Capture and Link-Inline software, together with the NTAPI/NTPL developer SDK, let applications capture, filter, and process network traffic at line rate with zero packet loss. The developer surface is a C/C++ hardware SDK (NTAPI) plus the NTPL programming language rather than a web/REST API; integrations ship as open-source additions to DPDK, VPP, Open vSwitch, Scapy, and Zeek via the napatech GitHub organization. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Smore
providers.description: Smore is a newsletter and flyer builder purpose-built for educators, schools, and districts, letting teachers and administrators create accessible, mobile-friendly digital newsletters from customizable templates to keep families and staff informed. The product emphasizes WCAG AA accessibility, translation for multilingual families, and engagement analytics on opens and clicks. Smore is now part of SchoolStatus, the family-engagement platform. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Smore publishes no public developer program, API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface — this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed domain security posture only.

providers.name: Callab AI
providers.description: Callab AI, built by Clusterlabs, is a cloud-based voice AI platform that connects directly to legacy on-premises PBX/SBC telephony (Cisco UCM, Mitel, FreeSWITCH) via SIP trunk integration, routing calls to AI voice agents with no rip-and-replace migration. The platform automates up to 70% of inbound and outbound call volume across support, sales, and scheduling, with no-code agent building, live human supervision and takeover, semantic knowledge bases, post-call transcription and sentiment analysis, CRM data extraction, and batch outbound campaigns. Callab AI exposes a REST API at docs.callab.ai for programmatic control of agents and calls. A Y Combinator Spring 2026 company founded in 2024, it serves hospitality, logistics, retail, and property management across three continents.

providers.name: Confide *
providers.description: Confide is a confidential messaging application that lets people communicate digitally with the same level of privacy and security as the spoken word. Messages are end-to-end encrypted, ephemeral (they disappear after being read), and screenshot-protected so recipients cannot capture or forward them. Available on iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, and Windows across 200+ countries and 15 languages, with a free tier for individuals and small groups and a Confide Plus subscription that unlocks unlimited attachments, message retraction, incognito mode, nicknames, and themes. Confide is a consumer product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained as a company record backed by GV in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Joya Communications
providers.description: Joya Communications Inc. is the consumer software company behind Marco Polo, a video chat application for asynchronous, personal video messaging with the people who matter most. Marco Polo positions itself as a privacy-first alternative to social media, with no ads, no public feeds, and no social engagement metrics, and offers a Marco Polo Plus subscription with premium features. Joya Communications is venture-backed (Battery Ventures) and, as a consumer mobile app company, does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Arrcus
providers.description: Arrcus is an AI-native networking software company that builds policy-driven routing, switching, and AI fabric spanning the edge, datacenter, and cloud. Its flagship ArcOS network operating system runs on merchant-silicon hardware and is complemented by ArcRR (scale-out route reflector), ArcIQ (analytics and visibility), ACE / ACE-AI (the Arrcus Connected Edge control and AI-networking platform), AINF (Arrcus Inference Network Fabric), and the TGAX AI switch. Arrcus targets GPU cluster connectivity for AI training and low-latency inferencing networks that reduce token cost. The company is venture backed by General Catalyst and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It exposes a login-gated customer portal and academy rather than a public developer API; no public OpenAPI, SDKs, or hosted API surface were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Distyl
providers.description: Distyl is an applied-AI company architecting the AI-native enterprise. Rather than layering automation onto broken processes, Distyl reimagines enterprise operations from the ground up with AI at the core, partnering with Fortune 500 organizations across Telecom, Healthcare, Manufacturing, Insurance, Retail, and Financial Services to design and operationalize AI transformations and deploy production-grade agentic AI systems in weeks. Its product suite includes Weave, Distillery, Context Mesh, Context Views, Journey, Personalization, and Apprentice. Founded by operators and researchers from Palantir, CIA, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Tesla, NASA, Stanford, and MIT, and backed by Coatue, OpenAI, Lightspeed, Microsoft, and Khosla Ventures. Distyl is a services/platform company with no public developer API; this profile captures its published web surface. Distyl is SOC 2 certified and GDPR compliant.

providers.name: Flannel
providers.description: Flannel is a simple overlay network that satisfies the Kubernetes networking requirements. It runs a small single binary agent called flanneld on each host and is responsible for allocating a subnet lease to each host out of a larger preconfigured address space. Flannel does not expose its own HTTP/REST API; it stores network configuration in either the Kubernetes API or etcd directly and is managed via configuration files, kubectl, and Helm.

providers.name: Lastro
providers.description: Lastro is a Brazilian proptech company building artificial intelligence for the real estate market. Its product, Lais (lais.ai), is a generative-AI platform for real estate agencies that engages and qualifies inbound leads over WhatsApp and other channels, then follows the customer journey from first contact through to a closed deal — covering property listing and management, marketing and lead generation, pre-qualification, visit scheduling, administrative service and strategic reporting. Human agents and the AI work the same queue inside Casa da Lais, the operator dashboard. Lastro reports more than 1,000 real estate agency customers, over 5 million people served and more than R$ 12 billion in sales volume (VGV) managed in Brazil. The company is backed by Prosus Ventures and QED Investors. Lastro publishes no public developer API; the only programmatic surface found is the Wix platform-provisioned site MCP endpoint on lastro.co.

providers.name: Multus CNI
providers.description: Multus CNI is a container network interface plugin for Kubernetes that enables attaching multiple network interfaces to pods. It acts as a meta-plugin that can call multiple other CNI plugins, allowing pods to have connectivity to multiple networks simultaneously.

providers.name: Replica Studios
providers.description: Replica Studios (operated by Replica Media Pty Ltd) built AI voice, text-to-speech (TTS) and speech-to-speech (STS) technology for creators, game developers, and software teams. Its platform offered an AI Voice Library of 40+ expressive voices, Voice Lab for blending up to five voices into a custom character, and Voice Director for generating voice overs and dialogue. Developers integrated these capabilities through the Replica API v2 (OpenAPI 3.0.0) — a REST API supporting text-to-speech, speech-to-speech, and voice-listing operations, authenticated with API keys or Bearer JWTs minted at the /v2/auth endpoint. Replica Studios was a Techstars portfolio company. The company ceased operations on 2025-06-30; the marketing site now shows a farewell page and the api.replicastudios.com host no longer resolves, so this profile is a historical/discovery record captured from public documentation.

providers.name: Observe.AI
providers.description: Observe.AI is a contact center artificial intelligence platform that deploys purpose-built AI agents across voice and chat to resolve customer inquiries end-to-end, assist frontline agents in real time, and evaluate performance at scale. Its conversation intelligence suite spans automated quality assurance, agent coaching, speech and sentiment analytics, and operational insights, with 250+ out-of-the-box integrations into CCaaS, CRM, and business-intelligence systems. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures, it was added to the API Evangelist network and enriched with its public trust, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Prodigal
providers.description: Prodigal is an AI company building purpose-built agents and intelligence for the loan-servicing and debt-collections industry. Its products include proAgent (end-to-end collections automation across voice and digital), PIE (an intelligence layer trained on more than half a billion consumer-finance interactions), proCollect (omnichannel digital orchestration), proScore (propensity-to-pay scoring from 500+ consumer attributes), proPay (an AI-native self-serve payment portal), proNotes (automated call notes), proInsight (QA automation, scorecards, and revenue analytics), and proAssist (real-time agent assistance). Prodigal serves auto finance, collections, healthcare revenue-cycle management, and lending, integrating with dialers and contact-center platforms such as Five9, Genesys, NICE, TCN, and DialConnect. It is backed by Accel and Menlo Ventures. Prodigal exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and compliance program.

providers.name: Kaizo
providers.description: Kaizo is an AI-powered quality assurance, coaching, and performance management platform for customer support teams working in Zendesk and Salesforce. Its AutoQA engine automatically scores 100% of support conversations in real time, analyzing sentiment and empathy, generating conversation summaries, surfacing escalation risks, and turning support data into performance insights. AI coaching builds data-driven improvement roadmaps for agents, while dashboards and reporting help support leaders compare team and individual outcomes. Kaizo delivers its product primarily as native apps for the Zendesk Marketplace and Salesforce AppExchange rather than as a public developer API. The company is SOC 2 certified, ISO 27001 certified, GDPR compliant, and continuously monitored by Secureframe. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Orchid Labs
providers.description: Orchid Labs is the company behind Orchid, an open-source, decentralized marketplace for bandwidth and a privacy-focused VPN. Orchid lets users pay for VPN service through nanopayments settled on a probabilistic payment layer built on Ethereum, using the OXT utility token and Orchid Accounts rather than traditional subscriptions. The stack includes an open-source multi-hop VPN client (Dart), the Orchid DApp for account creation and management, a decentralized directory of bandwidth providers running as smart contracts, and an L2/L3 nanopayment protocol. Backed by a16z, Sequoia Capital, DFJ, and Polychain, Orchid Labs focuses on decentralized privacy infrastructure rather than a conventional developer REST API.

providers.name: Whelp
providers.description: Whelp is an omnichannel customer messaging and support platform that unifies Live Chat, WhatsApp, SMS, Email, Telegram, Facebook Messenger, Instagram, and Viber into a single shared team inbox. It pairs a built-in CRM and unified customer view with a drag-and-drop AI chatbot builder, outbound bulk-messaging campaigns, and reporting and analytics for sales, marketing, and support teams. Whelp is backed by 500 Global. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Internet Assigned Numbers Authority
providers.description: The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) performs the global coordination of the DNS Root, IP addressing, and other Internet protocol resources. IANA maintains the protocol registries, top-level domain delegations, time zone database, and language subtag registry that the Internet relies on. Bulk registry data is published as machine-readable files distributed via rsync and FTP rather than through a public REST API.

providers.name: Robylon AI
providers.description: Enterprise AI customer-support platform spanning voice, WhatsApp, chat, email, social media and ticketing. The platform runs AI agents against a customer knowledge base with configurable personas, model selection, human-agent handover and assignment logic, and its APIs let external systems interact with Robylon and trigger workflows including voice and outbound automation. Documentation is public and extensive and the docs host serves both an llms.txt index and an unauthenticated MCP server; what is not published is a machine-readable contract for the product API itself.

providers.name: OpenEvidence
providers.description: OpenEvidence is a clinical decision-support search platform that uses generative AI grounded in peer-reviewed medical literature to answer clinical questions for verified clinicians. The product is free for U.S. licensed clinicians and is monetized through pharmaceutical advertising; partnerships include the New England Journal of Medicine, JAMA, NCCN, and the Cochrane Library. As of 2026 it serves more than 860,000 verified clinicians. OpenEvidence does not currently expose a public self-service developer API.

providers.name: Cloudgenix
providers.description: CloudGenix was a cloud-native SD-WAN (software-defined wide area network) company founded in 2013 and backed by Mayfield. Its AppFabric platform let enterprises build application-defined, policy-driven WANs managed from a cloud controller, with a full REST API (the CloudGenix Cloud Controller / AppFabric API) and first-party SDKs in Python, C#, Java, and JavaScript plus a CI-capable configuration CLI. Palo Alto Networks acquired CloudGenix in April 2020 for more than $420M and rebranded the product as Prisma SD-WAN, now part of the Prisma SASE portfolio. The public developer tooling remains published under the official CloudGenix GitHub organization.

providers.name: Nurix
providers.description: Nurix AI is an enterprise agentic AI platform for sales and customer support, delivering AI voice and chat agents that qualify leads, resolve support issues, and automate back-office operations across voice, chat, and messaging channels. Its products include NuPlay (customer-facing conversational AI agents) and NuStack (a workflow automation engine), backed by a library of 400+ pre-built integrations spanning CRM, contact-center (CCaaS), e-commerce/order-management, messaging, and scheduling systems. Nurix is backed by General Catalyst. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API surface — engagement is via sales/demo and pre-built connectors rather than self-serve API keys or developer documentation.

providers.name: SMTP
providers.description: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is the foundational internet standard for transmitting electronic mail across networks. Defined in RFC 5321 (October 2008), SMTP uses a command-response model over TCP port 25 (or 587 for submission, 465 for SMTPS). It defines commands including EHLO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, and DATA, along with a comprehensive set of response codes. SMTP works in conjunction with RFC 5322 (Internet Message Format) which defines the structure of email messages.

providers.name: CenturyLink (Lumen Technologies)
providers.description: CenturyLink is the residential broadband and home services brand of Lumen Technologies, a Fortune 500 telecommunications provider operating one of the largest fiber networks in North America. Following the Level 3 acquisition and rebrand to Lumen, CenturyLink's developer surface is exposed through the Lumen Developer Center and Lumen API Marketplace, which publish REST APIs secured by OAuth 2.0 for enterprise location qualification, quote-to-order, provisioning, billing, notifications, CDN and edge compute, DDoS mitigation, and Public Sector networking products.

providers.name: Nexthop AI
providers.description: Nexthop AI is a networking infrastructure company building next-generation, highly efficient AI and cloud networking for hyperscalers and neo-cloud operators. Founded by former Arista Networks operations leader Anshul Sadana, it designs scale-out and scale-across Ethernet switches, a networking software portfolio, and optics and cables engineered to lower the cost per token of large GPU clusters by improving power efficiency, cost, reliability, and speed of deployment. The company raised a $500M Series B led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Andreessen Horowitz at a $4.2B valuation and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio lead. It publishes no public web/REST API surface; this profile captures company identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Pindrop
providers.description: Pindrop is a voice and audio security company providing a continuous identity verification and deepfake-detection platform for enterprises. Its technology authenticates callers and video-meeting participants, detects synthetic (AI-generated) speech and fraudulent activity, and protects contact centers, virtual meetings, and connected devices. Pindrop's products span call-center fraud detection, passive voice authentication, and liveness/deepfake defense, and are delivered largely through partner platforms (Amazon Connect, Zoom, Webex, and others) rather than a public self-service developer API. The company is backed by Felicis, GV, and IVP and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Cometa
providers.description: Cometa (getcometa.com / cometaedu.com) is a Mexican education technology company that provides an operating system for private schools. More than 500 private schools in Mexico use Cometa to run and automate their operations across a set of integrated modules: Cobranzas (tuition collections with WhatsApp and email payment reminders and dashboards), Tienda en linea (an online store for uniforms, materials and services with vendor management), Admisiones y Reinscripciones (admissions and re-enrollment workflows), Comunicaciones (AI-assisted, multi-channel family communications with engagement analytics), Calificaciones (grade entry and SEP-compliant report cards and digital credentials), and Gestion Escolar (attendance, incident logging and administrative workflows). Cometa is a 500 Global portfolio company. It was surfaced as a stub in the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Cometa publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation surface.

providers.name: Eero
providers.description: eero makes home mesh Wi-Fi systems that are simple, powerful, secure, and reliable. eero pioneered home mesh wifi and sells products for homes, businesses, service providers, pro installers, and communities, including the eero Pro 7, eero PoE 7, and eero Signal, plus the eero Plus subscription for enhanced security and multi-network management. Devices are managed through the award-winning eero app and are deployed across 27+ countries. eero LLC is based in San Francisco, CA and is an Amazon company. eero does not publish a public developer API or first-party SDK; the eero app communicates with a private, unpublished backend.

providers.name: Inmarsat
providers.description: Inmarsat is a British satellite communications operator founded in 1979, originally as the International Maritime Satellite Organization, providing voice, data, broadband, and IoT services over a global L-band, Ka-band, and multi-band fleet of geostationary satellites. In May 2023 Viasat completed its acquisition of Inmarsat, and the combined company now operates Inmarsat's GX (Global Xpress), BGAN, IsatData Pro (IDP), and Fleet Xpress services alongside Viasat's ViaSat-3 constellation as a unified multi-orbit network. Inmarsat serves four core markets — Maritime (NexusWave, Fleet Xpress, Fleet One, FleetBroadband, Inmarsat C/GMDSS), Aviation (SwiftBroadband, GX Aviation, Jet ConneX, SB-S safety services), Government (L-TAC, GX, BGAN M2M), and Enterprise/IoT (BGAN M2M, IsatData Pro, IsatM2M, NB-NTN). Inmarsat operates a developer program at developer.inmarsat.com with documented APIs for BGAN network management, GSPS voice, Global Xpress, IsatData Pro messaging, Fleet Edge assurance, and Fleet Edge hardware replacement; access to interactive Swagger documentation is gated behind developer registration and approval, though the IsatData Pro Messaging API has an open-source Apache-2.0 Node.js client published on GitHub. Inmarsat is also one of the participating operators in the GSMA NB-NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) standards work for satellite-extended cellular IoT, with Viasat-led proof-of-concept code for NIDD (Non-IP Data Delivery) published under the inmarsat-enterprise GitHub organization.

providers.name: Manifest Law
providers.description: Manifest Law operates ManifestOS, a communication and case management platform for the legal industry, and is backed by Menlo Ventures. The platform exposes a standards-based OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect authorization server at app.manifestlaw.com, with an `api` scope for programmatic access and dynamic OAuth client management (`oauth_clients:manage`). This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Manifest Law's public discovery documents; no OpenAPI specification was published at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Salient
providers.description: Salient (Skwid Inc.) is an AI-native loan servicing and collections platform for consumer lenders — banks, credit unions, captive lenders, and specialty finance companies. It builds compliance-first AI voice and chat agents that automate servicing, collections, audit, insurance claims, chargebacks, and chargeoff workflows with native FDCPA, TCPA, and CFPB compliance. Its named agent products include Taylor (omnichannel servicing and collections), Marshall (automated audit), Flyn (total-loss insurance claims), Alex (chargebacks and disputes), and Melanie (chargeoffs). Founded in 2023 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Matrix Partners, and Y Combinator, Salient exposes a partner integration and onboarding API behind an authenticated developer portal. This profile was enriched from public web surfaces; the API reference is gated behind login so no public machine-readable specification was harvested.

providers.name: CarNow
providers.description: CarNow is an AI-enabled conversion platform built specifically for automotive dealerships, helping them turn more website visitors into leads, more leads into sales, and more buyers into lifelong service customers. Its product suite spans website solutions (AI-powered chat, digital retail, and shop-by-payment experiences), sales follow-up automation (Cruise Control, which prioritizes high-intent shoppers and automates nurture workflows), and service retention (Lane Assist, which drives post-sale engagement and service scheduling). CarNow works with more than 4,000 dealer partners and integrates with major OEM programs including Acura, Audi, BMW, Ford, General Motors, Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Land Rover, and Lexus. The company is headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina and is backed by Battery Ventures. CarNow does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs; its api.carnow.com endpoint is a partner/internal AWS API Gateway that requires authentication.

providers.name: Vodafone
providers.description: Vodafone Group plc is a UK-headquartered (Newbury, England) multinational telecommunications company and one of the world's largest mobile and fixed network operators, with operations in 15 country markets and partner-market agreements covering 40+ additional countries across Europe and Africa. The group serves 279 million mobile customers, 5 million business customers, and manages 215+ million IoT connections through its Vodafone IoT platform. Beyond mobile and broadband connectivity, Vodafone operates one of the largest IoT/M2M businesses in the industry, invests in 70+ subsea cables, and runs financial services like M-PESA (Africa) and Vodapay. Through Vodafone Business it sells connectivity, cloud, security, and managed-mobility services to enterprises, and through the GSMA Open Gateway and CAMARA initiative it exposes a growing portfolio of standardised network APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location, Match, MVNO Discovery, and more) via the Vodafone Developer Marketplace (developer.vodafone.com), which publishes 27+ commercial and CAMARA APIs across Identity, Mobile, Analytics, Boost/QoS, and Partner categories. The Marketplace exposes sandbox and live endpoints under api-sandbox.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com and api.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com, with OAuth2 (Consumer Key / Consumer Secret) authentication and Postman collections for every product. Vodafone is a premier member of the CAMARA alliance hosted at the Linux Foundation, a founding participant in the GSMA Open Gateway, and one of the principal telco operators driving network-as-an-API adoption globally.

providers.name: ARRIS Group
providers.description: ARRIS Group was a global telecommunications equipment company providing entertainment and communications solutions including broadband, video, and wireless products for service providers and consumers. ARRIS was acquired by CommScope in 2019, combining their broadband technology expertise with CommScope's infrastructure solutions. The combined company offers cable modem equipment, set-top boxes, network infrastructure, DOCSIS technology, and related telecommunications hardware and software platforms for cable operators, telcos, and internet service providers worldwide.

providers.name: Fortinet
providers.description: Fortinet is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Fortinet API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Insurify
providers.description: Insurify is an insurance comparison marketplace licensed in all 50 U.S. states with real-time API integrations into 120+ carriers (500+ across the carrier network), covering auto, home, renters, pet, commercial auto, life, motorcycle, and travel. Consumers get side-by-side quotes in roughly two minutes and can buy online or through licensed agents. Insurify's Evia AI agent (Expert Virtual Insurance Agent) is a voice-and-chat agent that handles end-to-end shopping conversations with bind-ready quotes and renewal-cycle re-shopping. In February 2026 Insurify launched the insurance industry's first ChatGPT app via OpenAI's app library.

providers.name: AtomBeam
providers.description: AtomBeam Technologies is a Moraga, California software company founded in 2017 that sells "Compaction" — a machine-learning approach to shrinking machine-generated data that replaces recurring bit-level patterns with codewords drawn from a trained codebook, rather than compressing bytes. Its Neurpac product is an on-premises, protocol-agnostic bidirectional compaction tunnel that reduces IoT, telemetry and file payloads by roughly 75% while encrypting and obfuscating them in transit; Neurcom and PCM are earlier-stage research products. AtomBeam licenses the software to IoT device and gateway makers, satellite and LPWAN operators, telcos, and the US Department of Defense, and has raised capital through Regulation A and Regulation CF crowdfunding on StartEngine. There is no public developer API program: the customer-facing surface is the login-gated AtomBeam Customer Portal (codebook generation and simulation) plus a Jira Service Management support portal.

providers.name: Nile
providers.description: Nile is a San Jose, California enterprise networking company delivering an AI-native Secure Network as a Service (NaaS). Founded in 2018 by former Cisco executives Pankaj Patel and John Chambers (chairman), Nile replaces traditional campus and branch LAN/Wi-Fi hardware-and-license procurement with a subscription-based, outcome-guaranteed wired and wireless network stack delivered as a service. The Nile Access Service combines its purpose-built Zero Trust Fabric (switches, access points, gateways, and sensors) with cloud-based autonomous operations, the Nile Services Cloud, Nile AI, Nile Nav, and Nile Digital Twin to plan, deploy, monitor, and self-heal enterprise networks. The platform emphasizes built-in Zero Trust segmentation, continuous performance guarantees (coverage, capacity, availability), and consumption-based pricing — marketed against 60%+ breach reduction, 99%+ ticket reduction, ~3x faster change management, and ~40% TCO savings versus traditional enterprise networking. Nile does not publish a general-purpose public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or Terraform provider; its programmable surface is limited to a closed admin/portal API and outbound webhooks used for documented integrations with ServiceNow (ticket and alert webhooks), Splunk HEC, CrowdStrike, Zscaler ZIA, Microsoft Entra (SCIM), Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Global Secure Access, Palo Alto Networks, Forescout (device inventory API), SecureW2, Aruba ClearPass, VeloCloud, Graphiant, Hamina, and Ekahau. Nile is available through the AWS Marketplace as a SaaS subscription.

providers.name: GoSky AI
providers.description: GoSky AI Inc. is a Taipei-based no-code conversational marketing and social CRM platform that helps creators, brands, and enterprises automate customer engagement across Instagram, Threads, and Facebook Messenger. Founded in 2018, its product suite spans the GoSky AI Chatbot Platform (build no-code chat flows, capture leads, and auto-reply to comments and DMs in minutes), GoSky Loyal (a digital loyalty and membership points program), GoSky Ads (precision ad placement across Google, Meta, and Shopee), and GoSky AI Customer Service (generative-AI-powered 24/7 support). The company operates a hosted SaaS console at platform.goskyai.com and reports serving 400+ enterprises including Mercedes-Benz, VOGUE, and Lazada. GoSky AI is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass GoSky AI publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: DriveNets
providers.description: DriveNets is a networking software company that applies the disaggregated cloud model to telco-grade and AI networking. Its DriveNets Network Cloud runs DNOS, a cloud-native distributed network operating system, across shared white-box hardware to serve core, aggregation, access, peering, DCI, and AI-fabric use cases. The Network Cloud AI fabric delivers Ethernet-based GPU-cluster interconnect positioned as an alternative to InfiniBand. Founded in 2015, DriveNets powers disaggregated backbones for operators including AT&T, Comcast, Orange, and KDDI. Device management is exposed programmatically via NETCONF/gNMI over OpenConfig and DriveNets YANG models, with a first-party drivenets.dnos Ansible collection for automation; there is no public REST API.

providers.name: DubClub
providers.description: DubClub is an all-in-one platform to create and join sports betting communities. It is a marketplace connecting sports betting content creators known as cappers or handicappers with subscribers who want timely, reliable betting picks and analysis. Creators monetize their expertise by selling picks and predictions through paid subscriptions, while subscribers receive content directly via notifications and messaging rather than scattered across social media and Discord. DubClub has facilitated tens of millions in payments for creators and delivered hundreds of millions of messages containing informational sports betting content. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital; DubClub publishes a consumer web product and does not expose a public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: Leona
providers.description: Leona is a healthcare communication company building an AI co-pilot for doctors and medical teams who run their practices over WhatsApp. Patients keep messaging WhatsApp as they always have, while the clinician side moves into Leona, where work conversations are separated from personal ones, categorized and prioritized, summarized for context, and voice notes are transcribed. Teams delegate chats by role, keep internal notes on a patient that the patient never sees, and reuse templates for repeated answers. Founded by Caroline Merin (CEO, formerly COO at Rappi), Tom Chokel (CTO, formerly CTO at Modern Fertility) and Arela Solis (Head of Operations), Leona launched publicly in December 2025 and serves physicians across Latin America. It ships as iOS, Android and web clients and publishes no public developer API, SDKs or developer portal.

providers.name: OpenDNS
providers.description: OpenDNS is a cloud-delivered recursive DNS and internet security service founded in 2005 and acquired by Cisco in 2015, where its enterprise capabilities now form the foundation of the Cisco Umbrella platform. OpenDNS continues to offer free consumer products - OpenDNS Home and OpenDNS Family Shield - providing recursive DNS resolution, phishing and malware blocking, and content filtering with parental controls across every device on a home network, all managed through the OpenDNS dashboard. Enterprise DNS-layer security, secure web gateway, and the Investigate threat-intelligence API have migrated to Cisco Umbrella (umbrella.cisco.com). Added to the API Evangelist network as a Greylock portfolio company in the cybersecurity sector.

providers.name: Outverse
providers.description: Outverse is an enterprise "service AI operating system" from Outverse Limited, a UK company backed by Seedcamp and Wing Venture Capital. Its platform lets support and operations teams deploy governed AI agents across complex customer-service workflows — email, chat, voice, and API-driven actions — from a single control center. Teams define logic, policies, and human handoffs in natural language SOPs rather than rigid workflow builders, and get observability over every agent decision, tool call, workflow path, and escalation. Outverse integrates with existing CCaaS and CRM stacks (Salesforce, Freshdesk, Genesys, Twilio, Talkdesk) and offers voice agents that verify identity, retrieve data, apply policy, and resolve calls end to end. The company advertises SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification and does not expose a public developer API at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Seedcamp and Wing Venture Capital.

providers.name: Bitstrips
providers.description: Bitstrips was a Toronto-based consumer software company, founded in 2007 by Jacob "Ba" Blackstock, that created the personalized comic platform Bitstrips and the personal-avatar app Bitmoji. Snap Inc. acquired Bitstrips in March 2016, retired the original Bitstrips comic product, and now operates the technology as Bitmoji. The public developer surface today is the Bitmoji Direct API (Bitmoji for Developers): an OAuth2 authorization-code-with-PKCE flow via www.bitmoji.com/connect that grants third-party apps access to a user's avatar ID, sticker packs, and sticker search, served from bitmoji.api.snapchat.com/direct. Note that Snap has deprecated the "Bitmoji For Identity" product; the standalone stickers and search integrations remain documented. This profile was surfaced as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company and enriched from the public Bitmoji developer documentation.

providers.name: LF Broadband
providers.description: LF Broadband is a Linux Foundation Directed Fund established in late 2023 that supports open source broadband networking projects, including reference designs and virtualization tools for broadband access networks. Its flagship projects, SEBA and VOLTHA, virtualize multi-vendor Passive Optical Network (PON) systems and are deployed by major operators such as Deutsche Telekom and Turk Telekom.

providers.name: LinkPeek
providers.description: Real-time website screenshot service that captures, stores, serves, and refreshes webpage snapshots via a simple GET-based image API. Give it a target URI and it returns a screenshot image.

providers.name: Rylo
providers.description: Rylo (Nagish Inc. d/b/a Rylo) is a New York-based accessibility technology company building free communication tools for people who are Deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability. Its consumer mobile app provides FCC-certified real-time phone-call captioning, in-person Live Transcribe, and Sign features, with automatic language detection across 50+ languages. Rylo raised $85M and is backed by Accel and General Catalyst. The company operates a consumer application only and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Achronix Semiconductor
providers.description: Achronix Semiconductor is a fabless semiconductor company specializing in high-performance FPGA (field-programmable gate array) products and embedded FPGA (eFPGA) intellectual property. Its portfolio includes the Speedster7t family of standalone FPGAs, Speedcore eFPGA IP for system-on-chip integration, VectorPath PCIe accelerator cards, and the ACE design tools suite for synthesis, verification, and optimization. Achronix technology targets AI/ML inference, 5G/6G networking, data-center compute acceleration, automotive, SmartNICs, and test-and-measurement workloads. The company is privately held and backed by investors including Battery Ventures. It exposes no public web/REST API or developer API portal; its developer surface is a hardware support portal, product documentation, datasheets, and design tools.

providers.name: Cignara
providers.description: Cignara is an enterprise AI platform that replaces traditional customer support (FAQ bots and IVR menus) with governed voice and chat AI agents that serve, sell, and grow. Its agents handle inbound and outbound phone and chat conversations end to end across 32+ languages, pulling customer context, applying business policy, executing transactions (checkout, scheduling, refunds, retention), and offering a real-time human copilot for support teams. The platform emphasizes in-region data sovereignty and hallucination-free, policy-bound actions grounded in each enterprise's own knowledge base. Founded 2026 (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) in San Francisco; legal entity ShopAdvisor Inc.

providers.name: MaxLinear
providers.description: MaxLinear, Inc. (NASDAQ: MXL) is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Carlsbad, California that designs radio-frequency (RF), high-performance analog, and mixed-signal communications systems-on-chip (SoCs) for critical network infrastructure, the connected home, and industrial and multi-market applications. Its products integrate RF, analog, mixed-signal, digital signal processing, security engines, data compression, networking, and power management into single chips that power cable and fiber broadband modems, Wi-Fi 6/7 and wireline home routers, optical transceivers, 4G/5G base-station and backhaul infrastructure, and high-speed data-center interconnects. MaxLinear exposes developer surface primarily as hardware/firmware SDKs and C APIs (for example the Panther Storage Acceleration SDK and the MxL890x Raw Acceleration API) delivered with its silicon, along with design tools, simulation models, and a technical documentation library — it does not publish a public web/REST API. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: Telephone and Data Systems
providers.description: Telephone and Data Systems (TDS) is a diversified telecommunications holding company providing broadband, video, and voice services across the United States through its subsidiary TDS Telecom, and wireless infrastructure through Array Digital Infrastructure (formerly U.S. Cellular). TDS serves customers in rural and suburban communities across 30 states, delivering fiber-based broadband and advanced connectivity solutions.

providers.name: Umony
providers.description: Umony is a London-based communications compliance platform, founded in 2017 and backed by Seedcamp, that captures, records, and archives employee voice calls, SMS, WhatsApp, and Microsoft Teams conversations at the telecom-network level for banks and other regulated financial institutions. Its platform spans the Umony App (BYOD softphone), Umony Mobile (eSIM carrier-level capture), and Umony Archive with AI risk scoring, and the company holds BSI-certified ISO 27001:2022, ISO 42001:2023, and ISO 22301:2019 certifications. Umony publishes no public developer API surface today.

providers.name: Caremessage
providers.description: CareMessage is a healthcare technology non-profit that operates one of the largest patient engagement platforms serving low-income and underserved populations across the United States. Since 2013 the platform has reached more than 20 million patients and is used by roughly 1 in 7 federally qualified health centers plus 200+ free clinics. Its products include 1:1 direct messaging, appointment lifecycle messaging, population outreach, health coaching, closed-loop referrals, Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) workflows, and Wellness Copilot, an AI-backed diabetes-management automation. CareMessage does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API reference; access to the platform is through its web application and a login-gated help center. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched from CareMessage's public web surface.

providers.name: LabLabee
providers.description: LabLabee is an AI-powered enablement, testing and troubleshooting platform for telecom teams, positioning itself as "the Copilot for Telco Engineers." The platform delivers on-demand, hands-on labs, sandboxes, learning paths and skill tests covering 4G/5G and Open RAN, IMS, network OAM, SDN and IP networking, telco cloud (OpenStack, OpenShift, Kubernetes, Docker), DevOps and GitOps automation (Terraform, Ansible, CI/CD), Linux, IAM and cybersecurity, and Industry 4.0 and IoT. Three AI capabilities sit on top of the lab catalog: AI Ask (search across telecom standards, vendor documentation and enterprise knowledge), AI Test (automated test execution and configuration validation) and AI Troubleshoot (automated trace analysis and root-cause identification). LabLabee serves telcos, universities, system integrators, network vendors and industrial private-network operators. Founded by Samir Tahraoui (CEO) and Mahfoud S. A. Mebarek (CPO), the company is backed by Accel, Kima Ventures, Reach Capital, Brighteye Ventures and 500 Global, and has been recognized as Best Telecom Startup by the World Communication Awards and with the TM Forum Growth Challenge Award. As of this enrichment pass LabLabee publishes no public developer program - no API documentation, API reference, OpenAPI, SDKs, CLI or public package artifacts were found on any of its surfaces.

providers.name: Prixtel
providers.description: Prixtel is a French mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) founded in 2004 by David Charles and headquartered in Aix-en-Provence. It is known for "forfaits flexibles" — mobile plans whose monthly price moves automatically between published tiers according to the data a subscriber actually consumed, with the ceiling known in advance — and it rides the SFR (historically also Orange) radio network rather than owning spectrum. Prixtel serves roughly 300,000 to 500,000 subscribers, reported about EUR 63.5M revenue in 2024, and was acquired by Altice France, the owner of SFR, in June 2021 for approximately EUR 415M while continuing to trade under its own brand; the Serena venture attribution that surfaced this profile is therefore a realized exit rather than a current holding. Prixtel publishes no public API, no developer portal, no SDK, no webhook catalog, and no machine-readable contract of any kind. Its only first-party software distribution is an end-user iOS/Android app for consumption tracking, invoices and line management; api.prixtel.com is that app's private backend and returns HTTP 404 on every probed path, including its own root.

providers.name: Sidechat
providers.description: Sidechat is an anonymous, campus-based social networking app for college students, built by Flower Ave Inc in New York City and backed by Canaan Partners. Students verify with a school email to join their college's private, location- and campus-scoped community where they post text, images, and polls, vote, and chat anonymously in a Reddit-like feed. Sidechat launched in early 2022, acquired Yik Yak in 2023, and operates primarily as an iOS consumer app. It publishes no official public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; this profile captures the company's public web presence and identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Harmonic Lightwaves
providers.description: Harmonic Lightwaves (now Harmonic Inc, NASDAQ: HLIT) is a pure-play broadband and video-delivery technology company headquartered in San Jose, California, founded in 1988 as Harmonic Lightwaves. It builds virtualized broadband access (the cOS platform, Distributed Access Architecture nodes, and fiber-to-the-x solutions) and cloud-native video streaming and processing (the VOS platform and VOS360 SaaS). Harmonic exposes a VOS REST API for media management, packaging, DRM, live event and linear-TV workflows, publishes first-party client-side ad-tracking SDKs for iOS, Android and Roku on GitHub, and maintains a technical documentation library. Its developer surface is largely operator- and customer-facing rather than a self-service public developer program.

providers.name: Highway 9 Networks
providers.description: Highway 9 Networks delivers AI Wireless Infrastructure as a Service, providing secure private mobile networks and deterministic 5G connectivity for enterprise AI workloads. Its Virtual Mobile/AI Cloud (VMC) platform combines a cloud control plane (Mobile Center), distributed edge running a 5G core and AI services (Mobile Edge), private 5G wireless infrastructure (Mobile Network), and connected device and robot fleets (Mobile Zones) to give autonomous robots, cameras, and edge devices ultra-reliable, ultra-low-latency connectivity across manufacturing, warehousing, higher education, and energy environments. Highway 9 exposes Mobile Center streaming APIs for orchestration, telemetry, device management, alerting, and analytics, though the full specification is available only through its partner portal for signed partners. The company is backed by Mayfield and was added to the API Evangelist network as an enriched provider profile.

providers.name: Lato
providers.description: Lato (LATO Labs) is a San Francisco company building an agent-native research and simulation platform for investors. Its agents source and conduct hundreds of voice interviews with verified domain experts and customers in any language, each returned with a recording, transcript and thematic analysis, then combine those interviews with thousands of documents from public sources and a fund's own proprietary knowledge into a single commercial study. The study becomes a live simulation of the market that analysts can question and run scenarios against to predict where a market is headed. Investors use Lato for commercial due diligence, expert interviews, market sizing, competitive mapping, customer interviews, pricing studies, deal sourcing, inbound screening and portfolio value creation, compressing research that traditionally costs hundreds of thousands of dollars and takes weeks into hours. The product integrates with the tools investment teams already run on, including Outlook, SharePoint, Gmail, Google Drive, Slack, Teams, Excel, Affinity, Attio, Harmonic and Granola. Lato was founded by Tymek Staniszewski (CEO) and Tien Chu (CTO), is backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026), and builds on Anthropic, OpenAI and ElevenLabs. As of this profile Lato publishes no public developer API, documentation or SDKs; the company surface is captured here for discovery and the repository will be re-enriched when a developer program appears.

providers.name: Open Programmable Infrastructure
providers.description: The Open Programmable Infrastructure (OPI) project is a Linux Foundation initiative demonstrating real-world use cases for offloading key infrastructure management services from host CPUs to DPUs and IPUs. It enables hardware-accelerated security, load balancing, and API gateway functions.

providers.name: swivl
providers.description: swivl is an AI automation platform built specifically for the self-storage industry. It combines a unified CRM and contact center that consolidates calls, texts, emails, and chats with AI agents for sales, billing, support, and review management, plus a tenant mobile app (Spot) for access codes, payments, and referrals. Its self-storage natural-language model is trained on hundreds of thousands of customer conversations and serves 3,500+ locations. Founded in New York City and backed by Techstars, swivl advertises open APIs and integrations with major self-storage management systems, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Astera Labs
providers.description: Astera Labs, Inc. (NASDAQ: ALAB) is a semiconductor company building purpose-built connectivity solutions for rack-scale AI and cloud infrastructure. Its Intelligent Connectivity Platform spans the Aries PCIe/CXL Smart DSP Retimers, Smart Cable Modules and Smart Gearboxes, the Taurus Ethernet Smart Retimers and Smart Redrivers, the Leo CXL Smart Memory Controllers, and the Scorpio Smart Fabric Switches, all managed by COSMOS (COnnectivity System Management and Optimization Software). COSMOS is the software layer of the platform: firmware modules on the devices plus platform-level libraries that run on hosts and baseboard management controllers, exposing what Astera Labs describes as a single standardized API for device discovery, configuration, security attestation, firmware update, telemetry, link diagnostics, RAS testing, scripting and fleet management. That API surface is an on-premises host/BMC SDK rather than a public web API: the COSMOS Developer Kit is offered through a "Contact Us" motion and the supporting application notes are released through a document-request form, so no public API reference or machine-readable specification is published.

providers.name: August AI
providers.description: August AI is a consumer health-AI companion that helps people understand their symptoms, lab reports, prescriptions, and medications, and connects them to licensed physicians through asynchronous, chat-based telehealth visits. Founded in 2022 by Anuruddh Mishra after a four-month misdiagnosis, August operates as a 24/7 health assistant available on iOS, Android, and WhatsApp, storing lab reports and conversation history in long-term memory to deliver personalized guidance. The service pairs a free AI symptom-assessment experience with paid online doctor consultations from board-certified MDs licensed across all 50 US states. August reports serving millions of users across 160+ countries in 30+ languages, and publishes medical benchmarks including 100% accuracy on the USMLE, 97.4% on MedQA, 99.4% on lab-report document processing, and 100% precision/recall on emergency escalation. It is backed by Accel and Claypond Capital. August is a consumer application and does not currently publish a developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Papernest
providers.description: Papernest is a French technology company, founded in 2015 and headquartered in Paris, that provides a digital platform for managing, switching, and cancelling household subscriptions — energy, telecom and internet, mobile plans, and home insurance — through a single interface. Built around the moment people move home, the service is free to end users and monetized through commissions from supplier partners across France, Spain, Italy, and the UK, having helped more than 3 million customers. Papernest does not publish a public developer API; it runs a private B2B partner integration program and maintains an official GitHub organization of archived open-source utilities.

providers.name: instabridge
providers.description: Instabridge is a global internet connectivity company operated by Degoo Backup AB in Stockholm, Sweden, and backed by Balderton Capital and Creandum. Its mobile apps give users access to a crowdsourced map of roughly 20 million free WiFi hotspots and to prepaid eSIM mobile-data plans covering 190+ countries with no roaming fees. With more than 200 million app downloads, Instabridge combines community-shared WiFi, pay-as-you-go global data, a data-saving browser, VPN, and cloud storage, and runs a distribution-partner program for prepaid top-up resellers. It is a consumer app company with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Petsapp
providers.description: PetsApp is a veterinary client engagement and practice communication platform used by more than 1,000 veterinary practices worldwide, with millions of pets registered and millions of dollars in payments processed. It gives clinics two-way SMS and in-app messaging, appointment booking, video consultations, digital payments, wellness and health-care plan management, automated reminders, and a lightweight CRM for building client relationships. PetsApp does not publish a public developer portal or open API; API access and documentation are offered privately to technology and PIMS integration partners through its partner program, and its public docs subdomain is a Jira Service Management customer help center rather than API reference documentation.

providers.name: Prepared
providers.description: Prepared is an AI-powered emergency response platform for 911 communications, now operating as the intelligence layer of Axon 911. Its assistive AI helps call-takers, dispatchers, and supervisors across the emergency response lifecycle with non-emergency call triage and deflection, real-time transcription and automated detail capture, live translation (40+ spoken languages and 200+ for text), multi-channel dispatch monitoring, and real-time quality assurance and training. The company reports supporting 1,000+ PSAPs (public safety answering points) and protecting 90M+ people, with claims of up to 50% faster call processing. Prepared is backed by a16z and General Catalyst and was surfaced through the API Evangelist venture-portfolio pipeline. The company runs a hosted dispatch console at preparedapp.com but does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: TCP/IP
providers.description: TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) is the foundational communication protocol suite that powers the internet and most computer networks. It provides reliable, ordered delivery of data between applications across diverse network hardware through a layered architecture of protocols. The suite encompasses protocols at multiple layers including TCP, IP, UDP, HTTP, and many others, defined through IETF RFCs maintained at the RFC Editor.

providers.name: Nexthop Systems
providers.description: Nexthop AI (Nexthop Systems) builds power-efficient AI networking infrastructure for hyperscalers and NeoClouds — scale-out and scale-across Ethernet switches, a networking software portfolio, and optics and cables engineered to lower the cost per token of training and serving large AI models. Founded and led by CEO Anshul Sadana, the company is backed by Battery Ventures and raised an oversubscribed $500M Series B in 2025 at a $4.2 billion valuation. Nexthop runs a public marketing, blog and news site plus a login-gated customer Support Hub and Learning Hub; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Aurora Networks
providers.description: Aurora Networks is the broadband and access networks brand of Vistance Networks, Inc. (Nasdaq: VISN), the company CommScope renamed itself to in January 2026 after divesting its Connectivity and Cable Solutions segment to Amphenol. Aurora Networks builds end-to-end access network infrastructure for global cable and broadband service providers: HFC and PON access systems, cable headend optics platforms, CMTS and CCAP gear, Distributed Access Architecture (DAA) devices, optical hubs, nodes and passives, RF and RFoG equipment, and video processing, security and delivery systems. Its ServAssure NXT family adds network performance management, alarm handling and service assurance software on top of that hardware estate. The brand originates with Aurora Networks, Inc., founded in Santa Clara, California in 1999 as a pure-play optical transport supplier to cable operators, backed by Battery Ventures among ten investors across roughly $60M raised, and acquired by Pace plc for $323M in 2013 before passing through ARRIS and CommScope. Aurora Networks is a network equipment vendor rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer portal, no public API reference, and no machine-readable API specification. Product and integration documentation, including the ServAssure NXT web service and message-bus integration surfaces, sits behind authenticated customer support portals.

providers.name: Earn.com
providers.description: Earn.com was a cryptocurrency startup founded in 2013 as 21e6 and later known as 21 Inc and 21.co, backed by a16z and others, which raised over $116 million. It began as a Bitcoin mining venture selling the 21 Bitcoin Computer, then pivoted to a paid-messaging marketplace where senders paid recipients in cryptocurrency to read and reply to email. Coinbase acquired Earn.com in April 2018 for a reported $120 million, and co-founder Balaji Srinivasan became Coinbase's first Chief Technology Officer. The standalone Earn.com product was retired and the brand was folded into Coinbase Earn, the learn-and-earn program. As of July 2026 the earn.com domain issues a blanket HTTP 301 redirect for every path to https://www.coinbase.com/earn, and no developer, documentation, or API subdomain resolves. Earn.com therefore has no independent API surface; any remaining API capability lives under Coinbase.

providers.name: enrich
providers.description: Enrich is a private, invite-only membership network for senior technology leaders — VPs, Directors, and CXOs from companies including Google, Slack, Anthropic, and OpenAI. It runs peer-led conversations with executive coaching, curated small-group and monthly in-person dinners, expert-led operator discussions, topic-based peer groups (organizational design, career transitions), and a private Slack community for real-time peer advice. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Cowboy Ventures, and added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead. Enrich publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface — it is a community/membership product, not an API provider.

providers.name: Flossy
providers.description: Flossy is a Santa Monica, California healthcare technology company that builds AI agents ("AI coworkers") for dental practices, veterinary clinics and med spas. Its named agents cover front-office and revenue-cycle work: Fiona handles inbound and outbound patient communication and scheduling across phone, SMS and web chat; Betsy scores call-center quality and marketing performance; Michael captures insurance, verifies benefits and surfaces billing insights; and Reid forecasts revenue and optimizes schedule capacity and staffing. FlossyHQ is the operator console the practice works in, and Agent Builder lets practices assemble custom agents. Founded in 2020 by Miles Beckett and Steve Seigel, Flossy began as a pay-as-you-go dental care marketplace and has since repositioned around agentic automation for practice operations. Flossy publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the one publicly reachable first-party integration surface is the embeddable Fiona web-chat widget.

providers.name: Open Voice Network
providers.description: The Open Voice Network is a Linux Foundation project advancing open standards for AI-enabled voice assistance systems. Its core initiatives around TrustMark and interoperability promote ethical, accessible, and interoperable voice technology across platforms and devices.

providers.name: VCNC
providers.description: VCNC is a South Korean mobile technology company behind Between, a private messaging and photo-sharing app for couples, and TADA, a ride-hailing and mobility service operating in Korea. A 500 Global portfolio company, VCNC maintains an open source presence on GitHub, including Haeinsa, a multi-row transaction library for HBase published on Maven Central. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API client SDKs.

providers.name: Fibraweb, S.p.a.
providers.description: Fibraweb S.p.A. is an Italian telecommunications infrastructure operator, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Perugia (Umbria), that designs, builds and operates its own fiber-optic access network for businesses, wholesale operators and public administrations. The company delivers FTTH/FTTB ultra-broadband internet access, dedicated internet access circuits, and local and long-distance voice/telephony services across the Umbria, Marche, Toscana and Lazio regions, with a proprietary network of roughly 1,500 km of fiber reaching 150 industrial zones and the ability to connect over 30,000 companies. Fibraweb is a Battery Ventures portfolio company (investors also include Equiter and GTD Grupo Teleductos) and holds ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27017 certifications. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; the company does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Execthread
providers.description: ExecThread is a selective, invitation-based network where successful executives discreetly share confidential, recruiter-led job opportunities with one another that are not posted on public job boards. The membership platform matches vetted senior professionals with unadvertised executive-level roles, offers executive branding services and resume review, and runs a points-based referral economy for members who contribute opportunities. Founded as a private career marketplace, it has been recognized on the Inc. 5000 and by the Financial Times. It is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners; it exposes no public API or developer surface as of this profile.

providers.name: Storyboard
providers.description: Storyboard is a fleet-operations AI platform that gives trucking and logistics companies voice-first, hands-free AI workers for their drivers. The system automates dispatch updates, driver coaching, safety alerts, and compliance monitoring (including hours-of-service and idling) so back-office teams field fewer phone calls and drivers stay hands-free on the road. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Santa Monica, California, Storyboard began as an enterprise podcast and internal-audio communication platform (a $4.5M seed round led by CRV in 2020) before pivoting to AI-powered fleet operations. It is distributed through in-cab telematics marketplaces such as Platform Science and ISAAC Instruments. Storyboard exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; access is via its web and mobile apps at app.storyboard.com. This profile was surfaced as a CRV portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Tagged
providers.description: Tagged is a social discovery and dating platform founded in 2004 and based in San Francisco, where members browse profiles of people nearby or worldwide, chat, play social games, exchange tags and virtual gifts, and make new connections. Originally a standalone social network backed by early investors including Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC), Tagged was acquired by MeetMe in 2017 for roughly 60 million dollars and today operates as a consumer brand within The Meet Group (part of the ParshipMeet Group) alongside apps such as MeetMe, Skout, and LOVOO. The current tagged.com is a consumer-facing web and mobile social-dating experience with no public developer program or API; a legacy REST-style API (tagged.com/api.php) that once powered third-party integrations has been retired. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Chelsio Communications
providers.description: Chelsio Communications designs and sells high-performance Ethernet network adapters and ASICs — the Terminator (T4/T5/T6/T7) Unified Wire family — for virtualized enterprise datacenters, hyperscale public and private clouds, cluster computing, GPU-accelerated computing and high-frequency trading. Its 1/10/25/40/50/100GbE adapters fully offload TCP, iSCSI, FCoE, iWARP RDMA and NVMe-oF onto a single chip with single firmware, and the sixth-generation T6 ASIC adds integrated cryptography offload for IPsec/TLS/SSL/DTLS. Chelsio distributes Unified Wire driver packages for Linux, Windows, FreeBSD and VMware ESXi plus the Unified Wire Manager management software as downloads from its service portal; it publishes no public developer program, REST API or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Firsty
providers.description: Firsty is an Amsterdam-based eSIM and mobile connectivity provider founded in 2023 that positions internet access as a basic human right. Its consumer app delivers free, ad-supported global data alongside affordable Classic (pay-per-GB) and Unlimited (daily/monthly) plans, plus international calling, across 170+ countries with automatic connection to the best available network and no physical SIM required. Firsty has surpassed one million users and lists partnerships with brands including Uber, Grab, Mastercard, KBC and Belfius. Backed by Speedinvest, it is a consumer travel-connectivity app with no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: DNS Coffee
providers.description: DNS Coffee collects, analyzes, and archives changes to root zone files provided by various top-level domains (TLDs), offering one of the most comprehensive views of the current state of the Domain Name System (DNS). By continuously tracking these changes, DNS Coffee uncovers valuable trends over time, making it a powerful resource for analysis and research. What began in 2011 with just 4 zones has grown into a robust platform that now processes data from over 1,200 zones daily.

providers.name: CesiumAstro
providers.description: CesiumAstro designs, manufactures, and tests full-stack communication systems and satellites for space, air, and ground missions. The Austin, Texas company, founded in 2017, builds active phased array payloads (Vireo), software-defined radios (SDR-1001/2051/2104/3104), reconfigurable processing units, SATCOM terminals (Skylark), tactical ISR/PNT payloads (Nightingale), and the integrated Element LEO satellite platform. Its hardware enables inter-satellite links, high-speed downlinks, lunar communications, and 5G non-terrestrial networks. CesiumAstro publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; this profile tracks the company as an aerospace hardware provider in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lightberry
providers.description: Lightberry is a San Francisco robotics software company (Y Combinator Fall 2025) that builds conversational AI "personality" software for humanoid and quadruped robots. Its platform lets a robot listen, speak, see its surroundings, and act on natural-language instruction without the owner writing any code, emphasizing emotional intelligence, contextual awareness, and autonomy rather than a simple speech-to-text voice pipeline. Lightberry ships pre-installed on robots sold through its partnership with Unitree, and the company runs a manufacturer-compatibility program with robot makers including Fourier, Booster Robotics, and High Torque. Its published documentation today covers device setup (power-on, WiFi provisioning, starting a conversation) plus an MCP architecture note describing a Model Context Protocol server that routes tool calls to individual Lightberry devices, which each expose a REST endpoint. There is no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI definition at this time.

providers.name: O-RAN
providers.description: O-RAN supports the Open Radio Access Network architecture under the Linux Foundation for more interoperable and virtualized mobile network infrastructure. It defines open interfaces between RAN components enabling multi-vendor deployments and network intelligence through AI and machine learning.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: EdSights
providers.description: EdSights is a student voice and engagement platform for higher education. It pairs an AI-powered SMS chatbot with real-time analytics to collect continuous feedback from students, surface persistence and well-being risk, and flag individuals who need staff intervention. Its Student Voice Score (SVS) benchmarks student satisfaction the way NPS benchmarks customers, and institutional dashboards help retention, advising, and student-success teams act on that feedback throughout the academic journey. EdSights serves 290+ colleges and universities and connects to campus systems — Banner SIS, Slate, Salesforce, Starfish, EAB Navigate360, and Pharos — via SFTP data feeds. The company is Techstars-backed. As of this profile EdSights exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhooks; integration is data-file (SFTP) based, so most API-artifact enrichment is not applicable.

providers.name: Mia
providers.description: Mia (Mia Labs, Inc.) is an AI-powered phone agent platform built specifically for automotive dealerships. Its conversational voice AI answers calls 24/7 across sales, service, reception, and outbound operations, handling appointment scheduling, service booking, lead capture, and recall/follow-up outreach over phone, SMS, and voice with automatic multi-language detection.
