Mia integrates with major dealership platforms and DMS/CRM systems including Tekion, CDK, Reynolds & Reynolds, and Dealertrack, and reports use across 350+ dealerships. The company raised a $20M Series A (roughly $29M total) backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Permanent Capital Ventures. This profile currently covers the company identity; no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: HTTP
providers.description: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is the foundation-level protocol for data communication on the World Wide Web, defining how messages are formatted and transmitted between clients and servers. It operates as a request-response protocol enabling browsers, APIs, and other clients to interact with web servers using standard methods like GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE.

providers.name: Kepler Communications
providers.description: Kepler Communications operates a cloud-based infrastructure network in space, delivering real-time connectivity, on-orbit edge compute, and hosted payload services for satellite operators and space missions. Its offerings include the Kepler Network for space-based data relay and communications, Kepler Compute for on-orbit processing, and hosted payload services that reduce the cost and technical complexity of operating in orbit. Kepler is backed by Canaan Partners, Costanoa Ventures, and Techstars. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been identified; services are accessed through the Kepler customer portal and an Atlassian-hosted support service desk.

providers.name: Mobileum
providers.description: Mobileum is a telecom analytics and intelligence software vendor whose Active Intelligence Platform delivers AI-powered decisioning, risk management, and network insight for mobile network operators. Its product families span roaming management (traffic steering, GlobalRoamer, campaign management), risk management (revenue assurance and fraud detection via RAID), network security (cross-protocol signaling firewalls and SMS/voice protection), testing and service assurance (5G, eSIM, IoT, VoLTE testing, dsTest), customer experience, and data insights and monetization. Mobileum sells primarily to carriers as deployed/managed enterprise software and does not publish a public developer portal or open API surface.

providers.name: David AI
providers.description: David AI is an audio data research company building high-quality speech and conversational datasets to bring AI into the real world through voice. Using a rigorous six-step research process (hypothesize, design, experiment, evaluate, productionize, release), the team produces datasets such as Converse (channel-separated two-speaker English conversations), Atlas (multilingual data spanning 15+ languages with dialect and accent metadata), Chorus (multi-speaker conversations for speaker separation and diarization), and Dialog (expert domain conversations). Its data is licensed to Fortune 100 companies and research labs working on speech recognition, translation, synthesis, and conversational AI. Access is arranged through samples, consultation, and a data license agreement rather than a self-serve API. David AI is backed by Amplify Partners. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Movandi
providers.description: Movandi is an RF semiconductor company founded by former Broadcom executives (CEO Maryam Rofougaran and CTO Reza Rofougaran) that designs 5G mmWave chipsets, RF front ends, phased-array antenna modules, 5G smart repeaters, and beamforming software for terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks. Based in Irvine, California and backed by Sierra Ventures, the company holds 130+ patents covering millimeter wave semiconductor, system, and software technologies spanning 5G, fixed wireless, and satellite connectivity. Movandi is a hardware/semiconductor vendor and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Prosimo
providers.description: Prosimo is a multi-cloud networking platform that gives enterprises a full-stack cloud transit, security, performance, observability, and cost-management layer across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle Cloud. Its Application eXperience Infrastructure (AXI) abstracts cloud-provider networking constructs and ties network transit, micro-segmentation, zero-trust policy, WAF, and observability into an autonomous, ML-driven control plane. Prosimo exposes that control plane programmatically through a first-party Terraform provider (prosimo-io/prosimo) for full lifecycle management of cloud gateways, network and application onboarding, policies, namespaces, and security profiles; a companion Pulumi bridge repository and reusable Terraform modules are published on GitHub. Prosimo was venture-backed by General Catalyst, WRVI Capital, and BlackRock; industry sources report it was subsequently acquired by Palo Alto Networks.

providers.name: rebtel
providers.description: Rebtel is a Swedish international communications company (Rebtel Networks AB, registered 556680-3622, headquartered in Stockholm) serving the world's roughly two billion international migrants with low-cost international calling, mobile top-up / airtime recharge, and calling cards delivered through its iOS and Android apps. It routes calls over optimized local phone lines to keep prices low. Backed by Balderton Capital and Index Ventures. Rebtel exposes no public developer API or SDK program; this profile captures the company's public web, legal, support, and security.txt surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: VeriSign
providers.description: VeriSign is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The VeriSign API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Volley
providers.description: Volley is a San Francisco voice-AI entertainment company, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, that builds voice-controlled and connected-TV games. Its catalog includes hits such as Song Quiz, Yes Sire, and officially licensed titles like Jeopardy!, Wheel of Fortune, and Family Feud, playable on Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Roku, Fire TV, LG, and Samsung TVs. The company is rebranding its consumer surface as "Weekend." Volley operates as a consumer entertainment product studio and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Crew
providers.description: Crew is a digital workplace platform for frontline and deskless teams, connecting frontline staff to corporate leadership across distributed workforces. The product bundles real-time team communication and employee engagement, labor optimization and shift scheduling, task execution, culture and recognition, knowledge management, a Command Center for administration and analytics, a compliance and safety suite, and third-party integrations. Crew reports serving more than one million frontline workers across companies including Taco Bell, Wendy's, Planet Fitness, and Harps Foods. It is backed by Greylock and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Discz
providers.description: Discz is a consumer mobile application that blends music discovery with social chat, styled as a modern, MySpace-inspired music community. Users discover songs, build music profiles, and chat with others around shared taste in music. The iOS app is developed by Discz, a Y Combinator-backed startup and a portfolio company of DCM Ventures. Discz publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its surface is the consumer iOS app distributed through the Apple App Store.

providers.name: Boardy
providers.description: Boardy is an AI networking agent — an "AI Superconnector" that facilitates meaningful professional introductions. Users message Boardy (via chat and voice) to describe who they want to meet, and it matches them with relevant people from its network, sharing contact details only after both parties explicitly opt in to connect. Boardy is a free consumer product backed by Creandum; it uses public LinkedIn profile information to facilitate introductions and documents its data handling in a GDPR-aligned privacy policy and terms of service. Boardy publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time — its public surface is a marketing site, legal pages, and an llms.txt for AI agents.

providers.name: iBasis
providers.description: iBasis is a global communications solutions provider serving mobile operators, MVNOs, over-the-top players, and IoT device companies worldwide. Its portfolio spans international and managed voice, 5G data roaming and roaming hub/breakout, A2P and RCS messaging monetization, and IoT connectivity built on eSIM technology, the Simfony connectivity-management platform, MVNO-as-a-Service, and fixed wireless access. iBasis also offers signaling and fraud security (FraudLock iQ360, Security iQ360, Signaling Vulnerability Scanner) and business intelligence for carriers. Customer and partner operations run through the eCare portal behind single sign-on; iBasis does not currently publish a public developer program, OpenAPI specifications, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV and enriched from the public iBasis web presence and live domain probes.

providers.name: P4
providers.description: P4 is a Linux Foundation project enabling programmable data planes in networking devices through an open, standardized programming language. It allows network engineers to define how packets are processed by forwarding planes of network devices independent of specific hardware implementations.

providers.name: Textsidekick
providers.description: Textsidekick (Sidekick) is a Y Combinator-backed (S26) workforce communication and knowledge-management platform built for frontline workers who do not have a desk. Workers text a question or report an issue over plain SMS with no app to install and no login; Sidekick triages the message, answers from company knowledge, converts issues into work orders, routes them to the right person, and captures every fix as searchable organizational knowledge. It also AI-generates safety procedures, handbooks, and FAQs, schedules preventive maintenance, and delivers text-based onboarding and training. Founded to serve the roughly 80% of American workers without a desk, it is live across 20+ plants serving 600+ frontline workers. No public developer API, SDK, or API reference is published at this time.

providers.name: Upscale AI
providers.description: Upscale AI is a pure-play AI networking infrastructure company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, founded by industry veterans from Palo Alto Networks, Marvell, Cisco, and Google and led by CEO Barun Kar. The company builds a full-stack, open-standards AI fabric spanning silicon, systems, and software — its SkyHammer scale-up ASIC architecture and NVIDIA Spectrum-X/SONiC-based scale-out Ethernet systems connect accelerators, memory, and storage for large-scale AI training and inference. Backed by Mayfield among others (Premji Invest, NVIDIA, Salesforce Ventures, Temasek, Tiger Global), it has raised $500M total at a $2B valuation. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interface surface beyond a Webflow-served llms.txt; it sells networking hardware and software evaluated by hyperscalers and neoclouds.

providers.name: OCUDU Ecosystem Foundation
providers.description: The OCUDU Ecosystem Foundation is a Linux Foundation project announced at MWC Barcelona in March 2026. It is an open collaboration hub dedicated to building a foundational reference platform for Radio Access Networks including AI-based algorithms, with founding members AMD, AT&T, Ericsson, Nokia, NVIDIA, and Verizon.

providers.name: Satellite
providers.description: Satellite IM builds privacy-focused, decentralized peer-to-peer communication software for crypto and web3 communities. Its core is Warp, a Rust interface-driven distributed data service providing end-to-end-encrypted chat, voice, video, and file sharing with data stored on IPFS. Uplink is a customizable decentralized chat application built on top of Warp. Satellite publishes no hosted REST or GraphQL API; the developer surface is the open-source Warp Rust crates and the first-party warp-wasm WebAssembly and TypeScript library. Satellite is backed by Multicoin Capital and its code is MIT licensed.

providers.name: Skyworks Solutions
providers.description: Skyworks Solutions, Inc. is an American semiconductor company headquartered in Irvine, California that designs, develops, and markets proprietary semiconductor products for wireless communications, automotive, broadband, connected home, industrial, defense, and consumer electronics applications. Skyworks is a leading provider of analog and mixed-signal semiconductors, with dominant market share in 5G RF front-end modules (35% market share). Products span amplifiers, filters, front-end modules, isolators, switches, and power management ICs serving mobile, automotive, IoT, and infrastructure markets. The company does not publish a public developer API but provides datasheets, evaluation tools, and design resources for hardware engineers.

providers.name: Aptos Orbital
providers.description: Aptos Orbital (legal entity Cryptosat, Inc.) is a space technology company, founded in 2021 and backed by the Techstars Space Accelerator, that builds integrated hardware for satellites and spacecraft. Its flagship Aptos Terminal combines space-hardened, radiation-tolerant edge compute (with proprietary SEU/SEL protection), persistent global satellite communications, and cloud connectivity to platforms such as AWS and Azure into a single device. The company advertises 5.5+ years of proven orbital operation, 99% global data coverage, and TRL9 readiness for LEO applications, with development licenses, engineering models, and flight models offered to spacecraft builders. Aptos Orbital was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes hardware brochures and a "start developing" onboarding form but no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Clubhouse
providers.description: Clubhouse (Alpha Exploration Co.) is a social audio application founded in 2020 by Paul Davison and Rohan Seth, backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Kindred Ventures. It popularized live "drop-in" audio chat rooms where people gather to talk, listen, and learn in real time across clubs, channels, and scheduled events. Clubhouse ships consumer iOS and Android apps and operates its service on the clubhouse.com / clubhouseapi.com domains. The company does not publish an official, documented public developer API or SDK; the only machine-readable interfaces are third-party, reverse-engineered clients maintained by the community and not endorsed by Alpha Exploration Co. This API Evangelist profile captures the provider's real public surface — website, legal, and support properties plus a live domain-security probe — with no fabricated API artifacts.

providers.name: Kiki
providers.description: Kiki (Kikihub) is a location-based social networking and chat mobile app that connects people nearby for local friendships, dating, networking, and community conversations. Users join local chat rooms to discover people around them and start real conversations, meeting new friends and matches in their area. The app is available for iOS and Android. Kiki publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation; this profile tracks the company within the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed (500 Global, a16z) consumer social lead awaiting any future developer surface.

providers.name: MeetMe
providers.description: MeetMe is a consumer social-discovery and chat platform that helps people find and connect with new people nearby who share their interests, through profiles, feeds, live streaming, and real-time messaging on web and mobile. Operated by The Meet Group as part of the ParshipMeet Group, MeetMe grew out of the myYearbook social network and today runs as a location-aware social networking and dating-adjacent app. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass MeetMe publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDKs — this profile captures its identity, legal surface, and live domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Skout
providers.description: Skout is a location-based social discovery and dating mobile app that lets people meet, chat, and make connections with others nearby or worldwide. Operated by the ParshipMeet Group, Skout is distributed as consumer iOS and Android applications and an in-browser experience, and was an early a16z portfolio company. It is a consumer product with no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or API surface; this profile captures its public identity and published legal/support pages. Added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: SpotHopper
providers.description: SpotHopper is a Milwaukee, Wisconsin based restaurant marketing and web technology company, founded in 2015, selling an all-in-one, AI-assisted platform to independent restaurants and multi-location restaurant groups. The platform bundles restaurant website design and hosting (customer sites are served from the spotapps.co domain), SEO and Google Business Profile syncing, menu / specials / event publishing, automated social posting to Facebook and Instagram, email and SMS campaigns, review generation and reputation management, and link-outs to reservation and ordering partners such as OpenTable, Yelp and UberEats. The company markets itself as powering more than 20,000 restaurants. As of the 2026-08-29 enrichment probe SpotHopper publishes no developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Altira Health
providers.description: Altira Health is a San Francisco-based healthcare technology company, founded in 2025, building AI-powered clinical follow-up for health systems. Its virtual clinical assistant, Lena, engages discharged and at-risk patients over voice and SMS, carries clinical context from the EMR across interactions, adapts across languages, escalates to human clinicians when needed, and documents findings directly back into the electronic medical record. The platform aims to recover clinician staff time and reduce hospital readmissions, and advertises API, webhook, dashboard, and analytics surfaces for connected EMR workflows (no public developer portal or API documentation is published as of this profile). Backed by Homebrew, Coalition, Focal, Stone Mountain Ventures, and Wireframe Ventures.

providers.name: Binu
providers.description: Datafree Technologies (originally biNu, founded 2008 and headquartered in Sydney, Australia) operates a #datafree reverse-billing connectivity platform that lets enterprises sponsor the mobile data cost of their websites, apps and portals so end users can reach those digital services without spending their own airtime or data - much like a toll-free number, but for the mobile internet. Widely deployed across South African mobile networks, the platform works on any device with no new SIM, top-up or contract, and layers on security controls, allowlist management, time windows, usage caps and audit logging. Products include the Datafree Platform and Datafree Connect. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Bloxtel, Inc.
providers.description: Bloxtel, Inc. builds a decentralized private 5G platform that lets enterprises deploy standalone 5G networks in hours. Its all-in-one 5G Access Point runs Open6GC, Bloxtel's decentralized network core, and pairs with tokenized dSIM electronic-SIM technology and a Web3 Operator dApp for configuring networks, managing dSIM subscriptions, and AI-powered predictive maintenance. Solutions span indoor coverage, SIM-swap protection, neutral hosting, peer nodes, and network analytics, targeting lower latency, reduced threat surface, and lower cost versus traditional carrier deployments. Backed by 500 Global. As of this profile Bloxtel publishes a marketing and lead-generation site only, with no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDK yet available.

providers.name: Rakuten Mobile
providers.description: Rakuten Mobile is the Japanese mobile network operator (MNO) of Rakuten Group, headquartered in Setagaya, Tokyo, and Japan's fourth nationwide carrier alongside NTT Docomo, KDDI, and SoftBank. Commercially launched in April 2020 and surpassing 10 million subscribers in December 2025, Rakuten Mobile built and operates the world's first fully cloud-native, end-to-end virtualized mobile network on Open RAN, with 4G population coverage of 99.9% and expanding 5G plus 700 MHz Platinum Band rollout. The same engineering effort spun out into Rakuten Symphony, a B2B business that productizes the Rakuten Mobile playbook as the Symworld platform — a cloud-native operating platform for telcos covering Open RAN (CU/DU/RIC, Symware distributed unit appliance), Symworld Cloud (Kubernetes-based hyperconverged telco cloud / CNP), OSS/BSS, site management, and a marketplace of pre-integrated cloud-native network functions from 50+ vendor partners. Symphony also offers Rakuten CPaaS (carrier-grade SMS, Confirm/OTP, and Short URL APIs running on the Rakuten Mobile network with JWT-authenticated REST endpoints at api.cpaas.symphony.rakuten.net) and Rakuten Communications Platform (RCP) for enterprise private 5G. Public, developer-accessible APIs are concentrated in the CPaaS suite; the Symworld platform APIs themselves are TM Forum-aligned but exposed under commercial engagement rather than a public developer signup.

providers.name: WhatsCookin'
providers.description: WhatsCookin' is a community cooperation platform — a "Cooperation Engine for Communities" — that helps people organize local and virtual gatherings and build healthy social connections. Members join or create Circles (community spaces for conversation and events), post Offers to gauge interest in potential events, and make Wishes that others can fulfill by hosting. Communities span wellness, community-building, language exchange, and food, with active circles in Tucson, Queens, San Francisco, and Oakland. It is available on the web and as native iOS and Android apps. Backed by Bloomberg Beta. There is no public developer/API surface at this time.

providers.name: Xsight Labs
providers.description: Xsight Labs is a fabless semiconductor company redefining AI and cloud connectivity with end-to-end, software-defined silicon for hyperscale data centers. Its X-Series programmable Ethernet switch silicon (X1, X2) delivers 3.2-12.8 Tbps with sub-700ns latency and is programmable through XISA, the first fully open, documented switch instruction set architecture, published under MPLv2. Its E-Series is billed as the industry's first fully software-defined 800G DPU family, placing 64 Arm Neoverse N2 cores directly in the data path and programmable with standard Linux tooling (XDP, DPDK, SPDK) with no proprietary SDK. Xsight Labs contributes SONiC platform code and a SAI implementation through its public GitHub organization. Backed by Battery Ventures among other investors. The company publishes technical documentation, XISA specifications, and programming examples rather than a hosted web API; no public OpenAPI, REST endpoints, or hosted API surface were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Brunswick Corporation
providers.description: Brunswick Corporation is a global leader in marine recreation and technology, headquartered in Mettawa, Illinois (NYSE: BC). Brunswick owns over 60 brands across marine propulsion (Mercury Marine, Mercury Racing, MerCruiser, Fliteboard), boat manufacturing (Boston Whaler, Sea Ray, Bayliner, Lund, Crestliner, Harris, Lowe, heyday), and marine parts and accessories (Navico Group: B&G, C-Map, Lowrance, Simrad). The company's ACES innovation strategy centers on Autonomy/Assistance, Connectivity, Electrification, and Shared Access.

providers.name: getriff
providers.description: Riff (getriff.co) is a voice and video workspace for remote and hybrid teams, backed by Balderton Capital. Its Mac and Windows desktop apps aim to reduce Slack overload and Zoom fatigue with a minimal video header, one-click availability-based chat, multi-screen sharing with drawing tools, advanced echo cancellation, and focus-time scheduling that updates status automatically, plus Google Calendar and Slack integrations. Riff ships as a consumer/team desktop product and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI; this API Evangelist profile captures its identity, legal, and domain-security surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital.

providers.name: Hi Marley
providers.description: Hi Marley is an intelligent conversational platform built for the property and casualty (P&C) insurance industry, delivering carrier-to-policyholder communication over SMS. The platform connects carriers, policyholders, and service providers through a single messaging fabric to streamline claims — including Conversational FNOL (First Notice of Loss) intake, Total Loss Assist for auto claims, and Workflow Assist for property claims — layered with AI coaching, sentiment analysis, and data insights. Trusted by 130+ carriers, including four of the top ten U.S. insurers across auto, property, and workers compensation lines. Hi Marley is backed by Emergence Capital and True Ventures. No public developer platform, API documentation, or self-service onboarding was found; the product is delivered as a closed SaaS to insurance carriers.

providers.name: Luzia
providers.description: Luzia is a consumer-facing artificial intelligence assistant serving 85M+ users across web, iOS, Android, desktop, and WhatsApp, with a strong presence in Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking markets where it ranks as the #1 app in several countries. The free assistant offers AI chat, image generation, PDF understanding, web search, and an agentic "LuziClaw" task mode, with a Luzia+ premium subscription adding advanced reasoning, custom AI characters, and higher generation limits. Luzia is a portfolio company of Prosus Ventures. As of this enrichment pass, Luzia publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Polycom
providers.description: Polycom, Inc. was a pioneer of unified communications and video conferencing, known for its RealPresence video collaboration platform, SoundStation conference phones, and Group Series and HDX room video endpoints. Polycom merged with Plantronics in 2018 to form Poly, which HP acquired in 2022; the polycom.com domain now redirects to HP's Poly product line. For developers, Polycom exposed the RealPresence Platform REST API (via the RealPresence Resource Manager and Distributed Media Application, later branded Clariti) along with device REST APIs on its VideoOS endpoints, enabling programmatic conference control, scheduling, provisioning, resource monitoring, and billing integration. Developer resources are now consolidated under HP's Poly developer portal.

providers.name: Zapia
providers.description: Zapia is a personal AI assistant built for Latin America by BrainLogic AI (a Uruguay/Silicon Valley startup), delivered inside WhatsApp and as native Android and iOS apps plus a Flutter web app at app.zapia.com. It engages consumers in hyper-localized, natural-language conversations to compare prices, reply to and transcribe WhatsApp messages and voice notes, organize calendars (with Google Calendar sync), make reservations, and discover nearby businesses using BrainLogic's database of millions of Latin American business WhatsApp numbers. Zapia runs on Claude via Google Cloud Vertex AI and has surpassed 5.5 million users across the region, backed by seed funding led by Prosus Ventures. It is a consumer (B2C) product: as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal — this profile captures its public identity and consumer-facing surfaces.

providers.name: Apparta
providers.description: Apparta is a Colombian hospitality technology company providing a reservation-management and guest-engagement platform for restaurants, bars, and dining venues across Latin America (Bogota, Medellin, Cali, Barranquilla). The SaaS product covers AI-assisted table assignment and floor-plan zoning, no-show prevention with prepayments and cancellation policies, a WhatsApp AI chatbot for automated bookings, CRM campaigns over SMS/email/WhatsApp, POS integration, branded booking pages and digital menus, and marketing connectors to Google, Google Maps, Instagram, TripAdvisor, and Facebook. Apparta is offered in tiered monthly plans (Basico, Standard, Plus) and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API or OpenAPI surface is published as of this profiling; higher tiers expose a WhatsApp Business API integration on behalf of venues rather than a first-party Apparta API.

providers.name: Belden
providers.description: Belden Inc. designs, manufactures, and markets networking, connectivity, and cable products and solutions for industrial automation, smart buildings, and broadcast markets. The company delivers end-to-end signal transmission solutions for mission-critical applications, including industrial Ethernet infrastructure, cybersecurity, and IIoT connectivity. Belden's Hirschmann brand is a leading provider of industrial network switches and management software with CLI, SNMP, and REST API interfaces for network device management.

providers.name: Zymbly
providers.description: Zymbly is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building a voice-first AI copilot for aircraft maintenance. Its AI agents automate the administrative half of a maintenance technician's day at airlines and MROs (maintenance, repair, and overhaul organizations): troubleshooting issues, looking up parts, retrieving technical documentation, and generating compliant paperwork so technicians can focus on the aircraft. Zymbly is a demo-led B2B product with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications at this time; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched from the company's public marketing site.

providers.name: Aerospacelab
providers.description: Aerospacelab is a vertically integrated satellite manufacturer headquartered in Mont-Saint-Guibert, Belgium, founded in 2018 by Benoit Deper. The company designs, builds, tests and operates small-to-medium satellites — its Versatile Satellite Platform (VSP-50, VSP-150, VSP-300) family plus mission-specific payloads spanning very-high-resolution and multispectral/hyperspectral Earth observation, synthetic aperture radar, radio-frequency sensing, and narrowband/broadband telecommunications — for commercial, institutional and government customers, with an explicitly ITAR-free European supply chain. It is roughly 90% vertically integrated across platforms, payloads, avionics and subsystems, has flown eight satellites in under three years, acquired Belgian space-optics firm AMOS, and is building a European satellite megafactory targeting 500 satellites per year. Aerospacelab publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; its programmatic surfaces (mission control, tasking, image-processing pipeline and data platform built under the ESA InCubed MultiSpectral Companion Mission) are delivered to contracted mission customers rather than to self-serve developers.

providers.name: Jive
providers.description: Jive (marketed today as "Jive AI" and owned by IgniteTech, an ESW Capital company based in Austin, Texas) is an enterprise collaboration and communication platform — a digital workplace that unifies people, knowledge, and content across departments and locations for large, often regulated organizations. Capabilities include collaboration spaces and group discussions, knowledge management with search and co-editing, personalized role-based news feeds, mobile and desktop apps, and engagement analytics. Jive originated as a venture-backed (Kleiner Perkins) enterprise-social vendor that IPO'd in 2011 and shipped a REST API plus an official Node.js add-on SDK. It was later acquired into the Aurea / ESW Capital / IgniteTech family.

providers.name: Pinger
providers.description: Pinger, Inc. is a San Jose, California mobile communications company founded in 2005 by former Palm managers Greg Woock and Joe Sipher. It builds consumer and small-business calling and texting apps rather than developer infrastructure: TextFree (launched 2009, the original free texting and calling app with a free US phone number), Sideline (a second phone number for work and privacy, with team number sharing, spam filtering, auto-reply and voicemail transcription) and Index (a dedicated business line with auto-reply, scheduling, broadcast messaging and payment collection). Sideline and TextFree have together been used by more than 100 million people. Pinger publishes no public developer program, API reference, OpenAPI definition or SDK — its integrations run the other way, with Index consuming third-party calendar (Google, iCloud, Outlook) and payment (PayPal, Venmo, Square) services. The one machine-readable artifact it publishes is an llms.txt information sheet on the Sideline domain.

providers.name: RealNetworks
providers.description: RealNetworks is a Seattle-based technology company that pairs AI-powered computer-vision and secure-communication products with its long-running consumer media brands. Its portfolio includes SAFR (facial recognition for security and retail loss prevention), Kontxt (AI messaging and voice security for CPaaS platforms, Telcos, and MNOs), GameHouse (cross-device casual gaming), and RealPlayer (media playback). Product APIs for SAFR and Kontxt are delivered through authenticated partner portals rather than an open developer portal; the historical Real Developer Program (developer.real.com) is no longer live, and no public OpenAPI specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: UpSmith
providers.description: UpSmith is a Dallas, Texas-based company backed by a16z that builds AI agents for home services and skilled trades businesses (HVAC, plumbing, electrical). Its platform texts customers to confirm appointments, follows up on cold estimates, responds to inbound leads around the clock, and reactivates dormant customers, syncing customer records, job details, and booking data with ServiceTitan through ServiceTitan's official APIs. UpSmith consumes partner APIs (a native ServiceTitan marketplace integration) but does not publish a public developer API of its own.

providers.name: All City Communications
providers.description: All City Communications is a Wisconsin-based telephone answering and call center service provider offering 24/7 live answering for businesses across many industries. Founded in 1979 (originally as a paging service), the company operates from Green Bay and Milwaukee and delivers custom call scripting, message delivery by text, email or live call patching, call recording with secure storage, a customer web portal for real-time call data, and detailed call reporting. It serves property management, home restoration, electrical / plumbing / HVAC trades, municipalities, home health and hospice, healthcare, legal, landscaping, and travel and hospitality clients. All City Communications is a service business and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Axamer
providers.description: Axamer is the company behind Menteo (menteo.ai), an AI-agent platform for restaurants and restaurant chains, focused on Latin America. Menteo deploys a team of specialized AI agents for marketing (WhatsApp and email campaigns), 24/7 WhatsApp order taking, loyalty and rewards programs, and customer service, integrating with existing POS systems, delivery platforms, and messaging channels to unify customer data and automate marketing, sales, and retention. Plans start from $149 USD/month with no long-term contract. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Menteo publishes a public marketing site with Terms of Service and Privacy Policy but no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: C2M
providers.description: C2M A.S. is the company behind Connected2.me, a consumer mobile messaging and social application that lets people create a profile, receive messages, and chat in real time with new contacts around the world. The app supports anonymous and identified conversations, following friends, and online-status notifications, and is distributed on both iOS (App Store) and Android (Google Play). Connected2.me is a consumer-facing product with no public developer program, API, or SDK surface at this time; its published surface is limited to the marketing site, the mobile apps, and its legal documents (Terms of Service and Privacy Policy). C2M was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: chatous
providers.description: Chatous is a consumer messaging application for random, anonymous chat with real people from around the world over text and video. It connects strangers by shared interests using topic hashtags, letting users make friends and start conversations across iOS and Android. Chatous is a mobile-first social product backed by Slow Ventures; it publishes a consumer website, privacy policy, and terms of service but does not expose a public developer API, SDK, or documented API program at this time.

providers.name: Dialup
providers.description: Dialup is a voice-chat app that revives the magic of talking on the phone by pairing people for one-on-one calls based on shared interests. It automates recurring, scheduled calls so users connect serendipitously with friends, communities, or complete strangers around the world without any manual coordination. Callers opt in with custom caller IDs rather than random numbers, and the free service is available on iOS and Android. Dialup is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company; it operates as a consumer social/communication application and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: i2x
providers.description: i2x is a German real-time AI platform for contact centers, built by i2x GmbH in Mönchengladbach. It provides live agent assistance that surfaces contextual recommendations during calls in under 0.4 seconds, including automatic detection of purchase signals and faster agent onboarding; full-coverage call analysis with automatic transcription plus quality, compliance, and sales-opportunity scoring across 100% of conversations; and voicebots for automated inbound/outbound telephony and virtual agent-training scenarios. The platform emphasizes DSGVO/GDPR compliance with EU-only hosting in German data centers, prepared works-council documentation, and EU AI Act alignment, positioning itself as an alternative to US-cloud-dependent conversation-intelligence tools. i2x publishes no developer program: no API reference, no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL specification, no SDK on any package registry, no public GitHub organization, no MCP server, no agent card, no status page and no pricing — the only commercial entry point is a demo-request form. A private, login-gated API host does exist at api.eu.i2x.ai serving the customer web application at app.i2x.ai, but it is undocumented and is not offered as an integration surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of hv-capital.

providers.name: Kik
providers.description: Kik is a freeware instant-messaging mobile app for iOS and Android, known for letting users register with only a username rather than a phone number. Founded in 2009 by University of Waterloo students and released in 2010, Kik grew to hundreds of millions of registered users and was especially popular with teens. It has been owned by MediaLab AI since 2019. Kik formerly operated a developer surface — the Kik Bot Platform at dev.kik.com — and the Kin cryptocurrency, but that developer/bot API platform is no longer online and Kik currently publishes no public API.

bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.
